article_title: Explainable AI for Predicting and Understanding Mathematics Achievement: A Cross-National Analysis of PISA 2018
citation: Liu Liu, Rui Dai. (2025). Explainable AI for Predicting and Understanding Mathematics Achievement: A Cross-National Analysis of PISA 2018. https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Explainable+AI+for+Predicting+and+Understanding+Mathematics+Achievement%22+PISA+2018
title: An explainable-AI workflow combining feature importance, SHAP values, and surrogate decision trees for interpreting educational prediction models
description: The article demonstrates an interpretability workflow in which complex ML models are explained post hoc: "we employed explainable AI techniques: we examined feature importance from the ML models and used SHAP values and decision tree visualizations to understand how each predictor influenced the predicted scores." Feature-importance rankings identify the strongest predictors per country, SHAP values quantify each feature's contribution to individual predictions, and tree-surrogate diagrams expose conditional interaction rules. The workflow is presented as balancing predictive accuracy with transparency for educators and policymakers.
requirements: Trained predictive models whose outputs can be post-hoc explained (feature importance, SHAP, surrogate trees), applied to a large-scale assessment dataset with a broad predictor set
constraints: The authors caution that even the best models explain at most about one-third of variance in individual scores, so predictions are best used to identify general risk factors rather than precisely ranking individual students
target_learners: 15-year-old students in cross-national large-scale assessment contexts (PISA)
target_learning_goals: Understanding and predicting mathematics achievement and its contextual drivers
examples: The article applied the workflow to PISA 2018 math data from ten countries, producing country-specific predictor profiles and a Figure 5 decision-path diagram of SES and study-time interactions
